newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-NOVOTNA DENIES HINGIS SECOND TITLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NOVOTNA DENIES HINGIS SECOND TITLE.

text.p: Jana Novotna ruined Martina Hingis's homecoming party on Sunday by beating her 6-2 6-2 in the final of the European indoor championship.
Ignoring a partisan Swiss crowd and a strength-sapping cold, Novotna needed just 63 minutes to collect her 12th career title and her second of the season.

The Czech completely dominated the clash, allowing the 16-year-old Swiss to hold serve just twice and shattering Hingis's hopes of a second tournament win to add to her triumph in Filderstadt, Germany, last Sunday.
Hingis appeared tentative and nervous from the outset and failed to hold serve in the opening set.
She looked like she might re-group when she held her serve to open the second set, but Novotna broke her at 3-1 and went on to clinch the match with an ace.
Hingis continues to inch her way up the world rankings despite the loss. She moves up one place to eighth.
With Sunday's victory, Novotna jumped three places to fifth, just one spot below her career-best ranking.
It was the 28-year-old's first win in three meetings with Hingis, which included a quarter-final clash at the U.S. Open earlier this year.

"I was much better prepared today then I was at the U.S. Open," said the fourth-seeded Czech. "I knew what I would do and what she was going to do. I knew I had to attack and not get into any long rallies.
"What I did today I did superbly," said Novotna, clearly pleased with the way she played. "Today my game was so perfect that there wasn't any aspect that was missing."
Hingis burst into tears after the match and blamed her collapse on fatigue and a gruelling schedule.
"I've been tired mentally and had trouble getting into the game," said the teenager, who made her professional debut at the European indoors two years ago.
"I was having trouble with my serve I don't think I'm as mentally fit as I was earlier. I might be tired from all the tournaments I've been in."
Half an hour later Hingis was back on court with Helena Sukova for the doubles final against Nicole Arendt and Natasha Zvereva.
